content_html:
Traveling by train to Machu Picchu is one of the most spectacular experiences in Peru. Along the route, you’ll enjoy Andean landscapes, Sacred Valley views, and the Urubamba River before arriving at the majestic Inca citadel. In this guide, we explain which companies operate the route, available schedules, and how to choose the ideal train for your trip.

Main route: Cusco / Ollantaytambo – Machu Picchu Pueblo
⏱ Travel time: 1.5 to 4 hours (depending on the departure station)
Type of transport: Tourist train

Train companies to Machu Picchu

Currently, there are two main railway companies operating the route to Machu Picchu:

PeruRail

One of the most well-known companies, offering several service categories:

  • Expedition: affordable and comfortable option
  • Vistadome: panoramic windows and onboard entertainment
  • Vistadome Observatory: panoramic carriage + open-air balcony
  • Hiram Bingham: all-inclusive luxury experience

Inca Rail

Ideal for travelers seeking comfort and personalized service:

  • The Voyager: practical and affordable
  • The 360°: wide windows and snacks included
  • The First Class: premium service with lunch and bar
  • The Private: exclusive carriage for groups

⏰ Train schedules to Machu Picchu

Schedules vary depending on the company and departure station:

Main departure stations

  • Cusco (Poroy or San Pedro – dry season)
  • Ollantaytambo (the most commonly used)

Frequency

  • Departures from early morning
  • Returns from Machu Picchu Pueblo until late afternoon/evening

Recommendation: book in advance, especially during high season (May–September).

How to choose the best train to Machu Picchu

To select the best option, consider the following:

Budget: options range from economy to luxury
Experience: panoramic trains offer better views
⏳ Time: traveling from Ollantaytambo is shorter
Type of trip: solo, couple, family, or group

Traveler tip: if you want great views and comfort without overspending, a panoramic service is ideal.

Best time to travel by train

April – October (dry season)
Better weather and clear landscapes
Ideal for photography

November – March (rainy season)
Greener landscapes and fewer tourists
Possible delays due to rain
